title: Opening another application cancels launching animation of previous application
line: Launching a second app no longer removes the busy indicator from an app that is still starting.
explanation: KWin kept a single launch-feedback slot: every new activation token overwrote the previous one and destroyed its plasma activation object, which told the task manager the first launch had finished. On window activation it also only compared against the last token's app id. The change keeps a map from token to feedback and ends a token's feedback when its window activates with that token (or a window with the same app id appears or is activated), leaving the other pending launches alone. Each pending launch also expires after the launch feedback timeout from klaunchrc (the longer of the cursor and task manager timeouts, 5 s by default), so launches whose window never shows up don't stay around.

commits.message:
xdgactivation: keep launch feedback for every pending activation

Only the last requested token kept its launch feedback, so starting a
second app while the first was still loading removed its busy indicator.
Track feedback per token and end it with its window or after a timeout.

BUG: 492448

media.caption: Master: Slow Konsole clicked, then Slow Dolphin 0.5 s later (shots ~1 s apart): from the second click on only Dolphin has the spinner, Konsole's is gone.
With the fix, same steps with the launch timeout at 30 s: both keep their spinners, and each ends when its own window appears.
Master: a launcher that never opens a window, with Plasma's timeout at 30 s and KWin's read at 8 s (+3, +12, +20 s): KWin never ends the launch, the spinner stays.
With the fix, same steps: KWin ends the launch at its 8 s timeout and the spinner goes away before Plasma's own 30 s timer.
With the fix: the never-opening launcher, then Slow Konsole (shots 2 s apart): Konsole's window ends only its own spinner; the other launch ends at the timeout.

review.text: Tracking pending launch feedback per token in KWin's XdgActivationV1Integration fixes the exact Wayland root cause without touching unrelated layers. Entries are cleared cleanly on token activation, matching desktopFileName window activation/addition, or expiry using the klaunchrc launch-feedback timeout, so pending launches are properly bounded and respect user settings. The diff, commit message, and multi-scenario visual evidence (concurrent slow launches, timeout expiry, mixed slow and never-opening launches) are solid and maintainer-ready (minor optional polish: clamp feedbackTimeout() to at least 1 s against invalid 0/negative config values).
